payload.acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] A PreToolUse Bash hook refuses a command where basicly release follows a semicolon, and names the fix: run the release as its own command.
- [ ] basicly release as its own command, or after && only, still runs.
payload.description:
## Trigger

When an agent runs basicly release in a shell chain, I want a hook to refuse it when a semicolon comes before it, so I can never cut a release in the wrong checkout after a failed cd.

## Context

2026-09-25: a scratch-clone proof ran 'git clone X && cd X && uv sync; ...; basicly release 0.18.10'. The clone failed because X existed, the cd was skipped, and the release committed and tagged in the base checkout. Nothing was pushed, and the proof then ran on the real commit.
payload.requirements: The refusal names the command to run instead.
payload.title: refuse basicly release after a semicolon in one shell command
